nodes.text: Are there infinitely many $n$ (or any $n>105$) such that $n-2^k$ is prime for all $1<2^k<n$?

#1142 : [Va99,1.7] number theory | primes The only known such $n$ are\[4,7,15,21,45,75,105.\]This is A039669 in the OEIS. Mientka and Weitzenkamp [MiWe69] have proved there are no other such $n\leq 2^{44}$. Vaughan [Va73] has proved that the number of $n\leq N$ such that $n-2^k$ is prime for all $1<2^k<n$ is\[< \exp\left(-c\frac{\log \log \log N}{\log\log N}\log N\right)N\]for some constant $c>0$. This is discussed in problem A19 of Guy's collection [Gu04] . There is also further discussion on the Prime Puzzles website . Erdős made the stronger conjecture (see [236] ) that that number of $1<2^k<n$ for which $n-2^k$ is prime is $o(\log n)$.
